channel.title: Stoke Club Music
channel.description: Articles from Stoke Club, the Newport Beach surf rock band.

item.title: The Mixolydian mode
item.description: What the Mixolydian mode is, how to hear it, and why Stoke Club, a surf rock band from Newport Beach, writes with it.

item.title: Polaroid and the Mixolydian mode
item.description: A walk through the chords of Polaroid by Stoke Club and the Mixolydian move that gives the Newport Beach band's best-known song its dreamy feel.

item.title: Polaroid chords
item.description: The chords to Polaroid by Stoke Club, section by section: verse, chorus, and solo, in the key of A at 125 BPM.

item.title: The silence in Polaroid
item.description: Polaroid by Stoke Club stops dead before every chorus. A look at the song's structure and why the silent prechorus works.

item.title: Crocodile Tears and the Mixolydian lift
item.description: How Crocodile Tears by Stoke Club uses the Mixolydian move, G up to A, to lift its chorus. Chords, structure, and tempo from the Newport Beach surf rock band.

item.title: Crocodile Tears chords
item.description: The chords to Crocodile Tears by Stoke Club, section by section, in the key of G. 93 BPM on the record, 97 live.

item.title: Famous Mixolydian songs
item.description: Well-known songs that use the Mixolydian mode, from The Beatles to Lynyrd Skynyrd, and how Stoke Club, a Newport Beach surf rock band, uses the same sound.

item.title: About Stoke Club
item.description: Who Stoke Club is: an indie surf rock band from Newport Beach, California, best known for Polaroid and for writing in the Mixolydian mode.

item.title: Your Friends, November 6, 2026
item.description: Your Friends is the next single from Stoke Club, the Newport Beach surf rock band behind Polaroid, coming November 6, 2026.
